title: Scalar endpoints and supported sources for uniformizer reduction
statement: Let l be prime, Y a scheme with Y, P=ProjectiveLine Y and W=diagonalSurface Y Noetherian, and l invertible on Y. Let E be a finite intermediate extension in the algebraic closure of Q_l, let pi generate the maximal ideal of its integer ring and let n be nonnegative. Let d be any integral diagonal Diagram [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-category, def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-diagrams]. There exists a scalar frame ScalarFrame for reduction O_E -> O_E/(pi)^(n+1): adjoint-normalized unit endpoints on all schemes, the two shifted Tate-line endpoints and supported-source endpoint [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-endpoints], canonical restriction/direct-image squares [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-scalars] with invertible mates on the shifted lines for q,p1,p2, and normalized supported sources for both quotient projections. The supported-source maps satisfy the two scalar-mate source squares. The frame contains no diagonal arrow, trace or integration identity; its right derived functors are the fixed canonical models [lem-diagonal-canonical-right-derived].

proof.text: For a flat internal module, localize its single complex. The K-flat transpose of the ordinary extension unit is invertible; the single-complex unit equation identifies its adjoint with the specified Endpoint normalization. Apply this to the regular module and transport by the unique ordinary regular scalar multiplication isomorphism. For the integral Tate lines, use actual spTwists_locallyFree, the signed-line tensor equivalence and the internal/section flatness equivalence. Pull invertibility of l from Y to P and W and then to their residue fields.

Apply the uniformizer scalar-square theorem to q, p1 and p2, with the three integral full right-derived models recorded by d. Its all-complex isomorphism assertion gives the three required shifted-line isomorphisms.

Apply the closed supported scalar-source theorem separately to the two projections, using the common regular endpoint. Endpoint normalization and faithfulness of the underlying module functor force the two resulting supported endpoint homs to agree, since their semilinear underlying maps are identical. Replace the second hom by the first and assemble the scalar frame.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph (1); K-flat endpoints, perfect uniformizer comparison, closed supported-source normalization; no projective-line cohomology is needed for these scalar-frame fields.

mathlib_searches.query: An exact realization of finite condensed coefficients and diagonal cycle classes under uniformizer reduction; scalar extension of a diagonal diagram preserving normalized traces
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits on perfectoid BDeRham and unrelated exactness lemmas; no normalized diagonal quotient comparison. Local library supplies integration_transport for formal assembly.
Twelve hits including rightDerivedUnique and rightDerivedDesc; these supply general unit-normalized right-derived comparisons, not the geometric endpoint or finite-normalization construction.

theorem diagonalUniformizer_scalarFrame
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Y : Scheme.{u})
    [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian (ProjectiveLine Y)] [IsNoetherian (diagonalSurface Y)]
    (hY : IsUnit (l : Γ(Y, ⊤)))
    (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l) (π : PadicAlgCl.integers l E)
    (hπ : Ideal.span {π} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (PadicAlgCl.integers l E)) (n : ℕ)
    (d : Diagram (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} l E.1) Y
      (fun X ↦ spIntegralTwist X l E)) :
    Nonempty (ScalarFrame (quotientMap l E π n) Y (fun X ↦ spIntegralTwist X l E)
      (quotientLine l E π n) (quotientLineMap l E π n) d)
